name: Reserve Bank of India
summary: RBI, Day 228. The RBI moved from 'draining liquidity, not defending' (22 Sep) to hiking and defending with every lever inside four days: repo +25bp to 5.50% (7 Oct, unanimous; stance 'calibrated tightening' 4–2; cuts 'off the table'; Q3 CPI projection 6.0%), CRR daily maintenance to 99% and OMO sales (9 Oct), and on Saturday 10 Oct a window supplying the oil companies' entire daily dollar needs from reserves plus FX-derivative curbs (no rebooking, $5mn threshold, a 20% cash FX Risk Reserve) — Bloomberg's 'strongest since 2013'. It worked on the price (rupee +93p on 12 Oct to 95.78; ~95.3 on 13 Oct) and costs reserves: $734.6bn (wk to 2 Oct), −$46bn in three weeks including a record weekly fall, against a ~$200bn net short forward book from the FCNR(B)/swap mobilisation. The 2013 precedent: the OMC window was withdrawn once the rupee stabilised — its withdrawal is the stabilisation tell. Next: reserves (16 Oct, 23 Oct — first full week of the window), CPI (12 Nov), MPC 2–4 Dec (sell-side: +25bp more).

recent_signals.headline: **Hiked and then defended — the full toolbox in four days.** 7 Oct MPC: repo +25bp to 5.50% (SDF 5.25%, MSF 5.75%); rate vote 6–0; stance 'calibrated tightening' 4–2 (Kumar, Singh dissent); CPI FY27 5.2% (Q3 6.0%); GDP 7.1%; basket $116.1 Sept; 'rate cuts are off the table'; next MPC 2–4 Dec. 9 Oct: ₹25k cr OMO sale; CRR daily maintenance 90→99% from 16 Oct (first since Jul 2013). **10 Oct (Saturday): OMC dollar window — 'entire daily dollar requirements' of IOC/HPCL/BPCL met from reserves from 12 Oct**; FX derivative curbs (no rebooking; $5mn undocumented threshold; 20% FX Risk Reserve in cash) — press releases 2026-2027/1305–1306. Reserves $734.61bn (wk to 2 Oct; −$46bn in 3 weeks; record −$18.34bn wk to 25 Sep); **net short forward book ~$200bn at end-Aug** (BS) — a large part of headline reserves is borrowed and owed back over 3–5 years. Trading Economics estimate: OMC dollar demand $10–12bn/month (unattributed). ANZ's Nim: removes 'one of the largest sources of demand… but will deplete reserves'. — CONFIRMED (RBI documents).

**THE RBI IS DRAINING ITS OWN FLOOD: ₹1 trillion September OMO SALE programme — ₹50,000 cr first tranche; ₹25,000 cr on Mon 21 Sep (3× bids); ₹25,000 cr on 28 Sep — to absorb a ₹6.05 lakh cr (20 Sep) liquidity surplus created by the FCNR(B)/special USD-INR swap mobilisation (FCNR(B) ~$132.98bn; total swap-facility inflows $143.596bn; Business Standard).** That mobilisation is why reserves are $780.782bn (wk to 11 Sep) versus the graph's stale $675bn baseline — a 2013-style macro-prudential action already executed. Consequence: the 10Y (7.065%) did not rally on Brent's −7.7%; the marginal driver of Indian yields is the drain plus the October hike. Hike calls: Citi (pulled to Oct from Dec), SBI Research (Oct+Dec), StanChart (50bp FY27), HSBC, Nomura; ICICI Sec PD/IDFC First: 10Y 7.25% by 31 Dec. MPC 5–7 Oct; decision 7 Oct morning. Weekly reserves −$4.924bn (FCA −$2.372bn). (Business Standard 11/14/21 Sep; HDFC Sky; Zee; Bloomberg 16 Sep; Outlook Money; TE) — CONFIRMED.

**The RBI's October decision is now priced as a HIKE by the sell-side: HSBC +25bp Oct AND Dec (repo → 5.75%); Nomura two hikes (headline CPI to breach 6% Oct–Nov); StanChart 50bp split; BS-cited survey 60/40 hike/hold. No emergency action; no new macro-prudential directive found this window. (BS 15 & 17 Sep; FXStreet/StanChart; Business Recorder) — forecasts REPORTED / data CONFIRMED.**

**The October cut is gone; the question is a hike.** RBI held 5.25% in August calling the outlook 'hazy'; with Brent >$100, a Fed hike priced, the rupee's worst week since May (94.49 → 95.69), FPI −₹13,138 cr and August CPI polled at ~4.9% (third month above the 4% target; food ~5.5%), economists see 'little room to cut' at the 7-Oct review and some expect a hike by December (Mint). India 10Y 6.96% (3-month high) also reflects expected RBI liquidity withdrawal with system liquidity >₹10 trn (Trading Economics). RBI is defending 95.5 without a clean break of the 96.5 record. No fresh macroprudential/NDF directives found this sweep (NOT FOUND — check for Friday-evening circulars). (Mint, Trading Economics — CONFIRMED data; CPI REPORTED/poll)

The June 5 stabilization package is being stress-tested as the rupee re-approaches Rs96 (95.79). It is WORKING on the channel it targets -- the G-sec FII tax-exemption ordinance eased India 10Y to ~6.90% (4-week low) despite oil up and the US CPI shock -- and NOT working on the one it can't (equity-flow appeal: FIIs still selling, May a record outflow). A clean debt-channel win; the FX/equity legs remain pressured.

**THE JUNE 5 MPC MACRO-PRUDENTIAL PACKAGE IS WORKING BEFORE IT SHOWS IN PRICES — CREDITED WITH STABILISING THE RUPEE OFF THE 96-97 LOWS AND EASING THE INDIA 10Y TO ~6.95-7.00% DESPITE OIL.** Beyond the 5.25% repo hold, the June 5 MPC bundled a regulatory toolbox targeting the capital-inflow constraint: FCNR(B) hedging-cost subsidies; concessional ECB swap windows; capital-gains/interest tax exemptions for FPIs in G-secs; and an expanded Fully Accessible Route (new 15/30/40-yr issuances). These are credited with the rupee's stabilisation — it fell 77p to 95.71 Mon 8 Jun on West-Asia escalation but firmed to 95.47 (Tue) / ~95.40 (Wed) on Trump's tone, holding clear of the 96-97 record-low zone, while the India 10Y eased to ~6.95-7.00% even with oil elevated. This is the central bank's regulatory toolbox working BEFORE it shows in prices — a STABILISING signal, the INVERSE of the late-May 'deep-in-the-toolbox-yet-rupee-won't-hold-95' stress signal. All RBI triggers stay watching (no emergency hike, 5 Jun was a hold, no fresh large-scale intervention print this window).

recent_signals.headline: **MACROPRUDENTIAL ESCALATION — THE RBI IS REACHING DEEP INTO THE REGULATORY TOOLBOX AND THE RUPEE STILL WON'T HOLD ₹95 = A STRESS SIGNAL.** The full intervention architecture is now stacked: **the $5B buy-sell USD/INR swap auction (May), ~$1B/day spot dollar sales, NDF position controls (April 1 barred AD banks from offering rupee NDF to corporates; partial lift April 20), bank Net Open Position capped ~$100M/day, and ~$700B reserves deployed.** Despite all of it — and despite operative Brent sub-$100, the oil import-bill relief that 'should' help — USD/INR sits ~₹95.68 and the rupee will not firm. **The mechanism / decision-relevant read**: the binding constraint is record FII outflows (~₹3.33 lakh crore FY26, Republic World May 28) + 15-year-low FPI ownership; intervention can CAP the currency but cannot reverse foreign positioning. When a central bank uses this much of its toolbox and the currency still won't hold ₹95 on an oil-relief tape, that is the stress signal — not a sign of control. **Structural picture unchanged**: room to ease from 5.25% remains GONE (cuts accelerate FII exit); >$38B of reserves burned since Feb 28 (from the $728.49B peak); the rupee printed an all-time low ₹96.96 on May 20. The next reserves print (May 30, week ending May 22) captures this week's intervention — the cleanest forward sustainability test.

recent_signals.headline: **$5B USD/INR SWAP RESULT — ~1.96x COVER AT ₹9.10 CUT-OFF: HEALTHY DOLLAR APPETITE, NOT FUNDING STRESS; THE DOLLAR-STRESS TEST CAME BACK BENIGN.** The RBI conducted its $5B three-year USD/INR BUY-SELL FX swap on May 26 (the auction the May 25 brief flagged as the dollar-funding-stress read). It received 254 bids worth $9.8bn and accepted 141 — a cover ratio of ~1.96x — at a cut-off forward premium of ₹9.10; near-leg (spot) settles May 29 2026, far-leg matures May 29 2029. The swap injects rupee liquidity into the banking system while the RBI takes in dollars now and returns them in three years. **The mechanism / decision-relevant read**: the ~2x cover and orderly cut-off signal HEALTHY bank appetite for dollar liquidity — NOT acute dollar-funding stress — a constructive signal against the backdrop of the rupee slide and the >$38B reserve drawdown since Feb 28. It pairs with the May 25 'rupee undervalued' jawboning as a coordinated liquidity-plus-verbal-support posture: low-cost, reserve-preserving tools stacked on the structural swap architecture. **But it did NOT turn the tape**: the US CONFIRMED strikes inside southern Iran May 25 'dampened hopes for a peace deal,' the crude rebound reversed the rupee's appreciation, and USD/INR gave back the May 25 firming to ₹95.68 (+0.4%, rupee WEAKER) by May 27. **Structural picture unchanged**: room to ease from 5.25% remains GONE (cuts accelerate FII exit); the all-time-low ₹96.96 printed May 20 (clawed back by off-market sales); the fourth fuel hike (cumulative ~₹7.5/L; no fifth hike this window) compresses optionality via certain core-CPI feed-through. The next reserves print May 30 (week ending May 22) captures this week's intervention — cleanest forward sustainability test. The swap + jawboning CAP the currency and read benign on bank dollar appetite; they do NOT reverse the structural FII/reserve overhang.

recent_signals.headline: **RBI 'INR UNDERVALUED' — FIRST EXPLICIT VERBAL-INTERVENTION NOTE OF THE CYCLE; RUPEE FIRMED TO ₹95.22 (-1.0%) ONE DAY BEFORE THE $5B SWAP AUCTION.** On May 25, with India open while US/UK were shut for holiday, rupee depreciation 'appears to have stabilised, aided by RBI commentary highlighting that the INR is undervalued' (Business Standard) — the first explicit RBI verbal-intervention/jawboning signal of this kind in the cycle. USD/INR firmed to ₹95.22 (-1.0%, rupee STRONGER), India 10Y eased to 7.03% (-6 bps), and India VIX collapsed -7.9% to ~16.5. **The mechanism**: deal-relief (US-Iran de-escalation hopes) + Brent <$100 (oil import-bill/CAD relief) + the verbal signal combined to produce the first clean rupee-STRENGTHENING session of the cycle driven by oil+deal rather than pure spot intervention — and it lands precisely the day before the **$5B 3-year USD/INR buy-sell swap auction Tuesday May 26 (10:30-11:30 IST; near-leg settle May 29; far-leg maturity May 29, 2029; injects ₹42,000-43,000 cr durable liquidity)**. Jawboning is a low-cost reserve-preserving tool stacked on top of the spot intervention + structural swap architecture. **Regime read**: Tuesday's swap-auction cut-off + subscription = the market read on dollar-funding stress under the reserves drawdown; the next reserves print May 30 (week ending May 22) will capture this week's ~$5B intervention. **Structural picture unchanged**: room to ease from 5.25% remains GONE (cuts accelerate FII exit); the FOURTH fuel hike (₹2.61-2.71/L May 25, cumulative ~₹7.5/L) compresses optionality further via certain core-CPI feed-through; Bank Nifty +2.3% Monday is a relief-day bounce, not a reversal of the cumulative defense MTM cost. The verbal intervention is real and notable, but it caps the currency — it does not reverse the structural FII/reserve overhang.

On 17 Jul he said 'Inflation is under control, though there has been a slight increase now', reaffirmed inflation control as the PRIMARY mandate with growth secondary under flexible inflation targeting, and repeated his 5 June conditional — the RBI **will act more aggressively only if fuel costs become GENERALISED into wages and services, and is NOT prepared to tighten on oil-driven price pressure alone.** Repo unchanged at 5.25% after 125bps of cuts since Feb 2025 and three consecutive holds. **Next MPC 3-5 August.** Supporting the bond market: PSU banks bought Rs156bn of G-Secs over three sessions and India 10Y eased ~5bps to ~6.74%, with economists projecting July CPI slowing to ~4.0% from June's 4.38%. The under-appreciated flow: FPIs bought >$4.2bn of FAR bonds since 1 June. CONFIRMED.

**The RBI is shifting from spot defence to inflow engineering — and has briefed a wire service that it is rethinking intervention.** It mobilised **$20.72bn under its forex swap/FCNR(B) facility as of 17 July**, with bankers expecting a stronger mop-up through September — recouping roughly **39% of the ~$53bn war-related reserve drawdown via a liability-side facility.** Reuters, 21 July: 'Indian rupee's return to near-record lows reflects **RBI debate on intervention**,' with a syndicated line that the RBI is **limiting** intervention. State-run banks were seen cushioning Monday's move — the classic PSU-proxy signature. **Assessment: an internal debate about whether to keep burning reserves is now being briefed publicly, which softens the 96.52 floor.** Governor Malhotra's 17 July line stands unchanged — inflation is the primary mandate, and the RBI will not tighten on oil alone unless it becomes 'generalised' into wages and services. Repo 5.25%; **next MPC 3-5 August.** ⚠️ **The 24 July WSS release — the same day as the tariff cliff — will contain both the 13-17 July intervention and possibly part of the swap inflow; expect the headline reserves number to flatter the underlying spot defence.** CONFIRMED (RBI-sourced) / REPORTED (the intervention debate).

The RBI is holding the rupee AT its 96.52 record with borrowed dollars, not spot reserves: ET reports it is using the $20.72bn dollar-deposit/FCNR(B) surge to CUT its FX forward book (unwinding forwards), while briefing Reuters it is debating LIMITING intervention. No new on-record RBI statement in-window. The tactic preserves headline reserves at the cost of a larger forward liability that reverses on maturity — so the 24 July weekly reserves release (same day as the tariff cliff) will look better than the underlying spot defence warrants. Repo 5.25%; next MPC 3-5 August. CONFIRMED (ET-reported).
